note: Seeded breaks of the rules the Elements of Style brief names: comma splices, a missing serial comma, dangling participles, negative form, passive voice, vague abstract wording, separated related words, non-parallel lists, a succession of loose sentences, a paragraph that strays from its topic, and a tense shift in a summary. Every other series in these documents uses the serial comma, so the seeded one stands out.

inventory-count-memo.md.quote: The count started at 6 a.m., most teams finished by noon.
inventory-count-memo.md.issue: Comma splice: two independent clauses joined by a comma.
Missing serial comma before "and" in a series of three.

inventory-count-memo.md.quote: There were some issues with various aspects of the process in certain areas.
inventory-count-memo.md.issue: Vague, abstract wording; say which problems occurred and where.

inventory-count-memo.md.quote: The team started late, and the scanners there lost signal
inventory-count-memo.md.issue: A string of loose clauses joined by "and"; recast the paragraph into varied, tighter sentences.

inventory-count-memo.md.quote: Walking the aisles after the count, several mislabeled bins were found by the supervisors.
inventory-count-memo.md.issue: Dangling participle: the bins were not walking the aisles; make the supervisors the subject (which also removes the passive).
Negative form; "forgot to lock" is direct.

inventory-count-memo.md.quote: A decision was made by the managers to delay Monday's shipping
inventory-count-memo.md.issue: Passive voice; "The managers decided to delay Monday's shipping."

inventory-count-memo.md.quote: training new staff a week before the count
inventory-count-memo.md.issue: List items are not parallel ("order", "training", "the count should start"); start each with a verb.

winter-garden-howto.md.quote: spent annuals, diseased leaves and fallen fruit
winter-garden-howto.md.issue: Missing serial comma before "and" in a series of three.

winter-garden-howto.md.quote: Leave healthy seed heads standing, birds feed on them through the winter.
winter-garden-howto.md.issue: Comma splice: two independent clauses joined by a comma.

winter-garden-howto.md.quote: The gardener, after the first hard frost, once the leaves have dropped, should cut
winter-garden-howto.md.issue: Two interrupting phrases separate the subject from its verb; keep related words together ("After the first hard frost, once the leaves have dropped, cut...").

winter-garden-howto.md.quote: Having cleared the beds, compost should be spread two inches deep over the soil.
winter-garden-howto.md.issue: Dangling participle: the compost did not clear the beds; make the reader the subject ("Having cleared the beds, spread compost...").

winter-garden-howto.md.quote: Beginners often do not pay attention to drainage.
Mulch protects roots from frost, keeps weeds down, and the soil stays moist.
winter-garden-howto.md.issue: Coordinate ideas not in similar form; the third item breaks the pattern ("and keeps the soil moist").

winter-garden-howto.md.quote: Your shears and loppers should be cleaned and oiled before you hang them up for the winter.
winter-garden-howto.md.issue: A sentence about tools interrupts the paragraph on mulch; the paragraph should keep to one topic, so move it to its own paragraph or section.

winter-garden-howto.md.quote: Results will depend on a variety of factors.
winter-garden-howto.md.issue: Vague, abstract wording; name the factors or cut the sentence.

book-club-notes.md.quote: A vote was held by the group in March
book-club-notes.md.issue: Passive voice; "In March the group voted for The Salt Road by a wide margin."

book-club-notes.md.quote: Tobin fell ill near the coast
book-club-notes.md.issue: The summary shifts from present tense to past tense halfway through; keep the whole summary in one tense.

book-club-notes.md.quote: Most of us admired the writing, the plot moved too slowly in the middle.
book-club-notes.md.issue: Comma splice: two independent clauses joined by a comma.

book-club-notes.md.quote: the salt pans, the press gang and the coastal storms
book-club-notes.md.issue: Missing serial comma before "and" in a series of three.

book-club-notes.md.quote: did not pay attention to the map
Reading the final chapter, the ending felt rushed to many of us.
book-club-notes.md.issue: Dangling participle: the ending was not reading the chapter; make the readers the subject.

book-club-notes.md.quote: The book deals with a number of important themes in various interesting ways.
book-club-notes.md.issue: Vague, abstract wording; name the themes and what the book does with them.
